newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ENGLAND PREPARE FOR TEST AGAINST THE BEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND PREPARE FOR TEST AGAINST THE BEST.

text.p: The last time England played Brazil they were unbeaten for 10 games but came crashing down to earth as the world champions won 3-1 at Wembley Stadium.

That was in June 1995 and in the two years and 22 matches since then England have lost only once in open play -- when World Cup runners-up Italy beat them 1-0 at Wembley in a World Cup qualifier four months ago.

England showed a vast improvement to beat Italy 2-0 in their opening match in the Tournoi de France last Wednesday, and made it six wins in a row when they defeated France 1-0 in Montpellier on Saturday.
They now have a chance to measure their recent progress against the best, already assured of finishing first in the tournament following Italy's 3-3 draw with Brazil in Lyon on Sunday.

A win against Brazil -- even in a semi-friendly tournament such as this one -- would convince even the most sceptical observer England are within touching distance of providing a serious threat in the World Cup finals starting exactly a year to the day after Tuesday's match at the Parc des Princes.

England skipper Alan Shearer is under no illusions of the task ahead -- even if England have been re-writing their record books in the last 10 days -- winning in Poland for the first time in 31 years, beating Italy for the first time in 20 years and winning in France for the first time in 48 years.

If they beat Brazil they would have won seven successive matches for the first time since 1966, but the world champions will be determined to win for the first time on their current European tour after losing 4-2 to Norway at the end of May and then drawing 1-1 with France and 3-3 with the Italians.

Their coach Mario Zagallo said on Sunday: "England are traditionally one of the strongest teams in the world, but have not achieved as much as they should have. They seem to be improving now, and a strong England is good for the game. We expect a hard match, and will be trying just as hard to beat them."

England and Brazil have met each other only 18 times in 41 years -- and 15 of those games have ended in draws or Brazilian victories. England won only in 1956, 1984 and 1990, but their confidence is sky-high and they will be desperate to finish the international season with their seventh successive win.

England manager Glenn Hoddle has injury worries over Robert Lee (foot), David Batty (leg muscle), Paul Scholes (hamstring), Martin Keown (arm) and goalkeeper David Seaman (ankle), while skipper Alan Shearer has a slight ankle strain but should be fit, even though neither he or Seaman trained on Monday.
Midfielder David Beckham is suspended after being booked against Italy and France but midfielder Paul Gascoigne is fit and should earn his 51st cap.
It will be the perfect stage for Gascoigne to show he still has a significant role to play for England.

Hoddle said: "We're playing the best side in the world and the fact we are up against Brazil is enough to inspire the players. These are the sort of games we look forward to as a player and a coach and while we are delighted to be playing them, we are not scared of them."
Brazil will be without suspended defender Mauro Silva, who is likely to be replaced by Flavio Conceicao.
There will be a fascinating sub-plot to the match with Shearer leading the England attack and Ronaldo, who is poised to replace him as the world's most expensive signing, leading the Brazilian line.
The Tournoi de France has produced four outstanding matches -- and another one is certainly on the cards on Tuesday.
Teams:
England (probable): David Seaman; Gary Neville, Gareth Southgate, Sol Campbell, Philip Neville, Paul Gascoigne, Paul Scholes, Paul Ince, Graeme Le Saux, Teddy Sheringham, Alan Shearer.
Brazil: Taffarel; Cafu, Celio Silva, Aldair, Roberto Carlos, Flavio Conceicao, Dunga, Denilson, Leonardo, Romario, Ronaldo.
Referee: John Jairo Toro Rendon (Colombia).
